Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

disorder noun

lack of order, confusion

also chaos, turmoil, confusion (disorder), in disorder, unrest, uproar, be in an uproar

classical

Caes. BG 3.28: magna tōtīus exercitūs perturbātiō facta est (Lewis & Short)
Cic. N.D. 1.3 (Lewis & Short)

perturbātiō, perturbātiōnis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

confusion, disorder; unrest

Disorder in a crowd, an army or the state; of the mind, agitation, emotion (Cic.) (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • cōnfūsiō, cōnfūsiōnis f. — a confounding, confusion, disorder

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. N.D. 1.3: perturbātiō et cōnfūsiō vītae (Lewis & Short); Cic. Off. 2.65: temporum (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

  • tumultus, tumultūs m. — uproar, commotion, unrest

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 2.11: magnō cum strepitū ac tumultū (Lewis & Short); Traupman 400 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Noisy disorder, a riot; in Roman law a sudden war or rising near home (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • magna tōtīus exercitūs perturbātiō facta est

    there was great disorder throughout the armyCaes. BG 3.28 (Lewis & Short)

  • quid hoc hīc clāmōris, quid hoc hīc tumultī est?

    what is all this shouting, what is all this uproar here?Enn. Trag. 204 (Lewis & Short)

  • tumultuārī

    to be in an uproarCic. Agr. 2.101 (Lewis & Short s.v. tumultuor); Traupman 400

See also confuse, disease, mix.
